svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: a framework update removes retired linters and preserves project controls
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: a framework update removes retired linters and preserves project controls
A settings file linked outside the project stops the update
Without the link, the update arrives as a clean merge request

g.text: Given the main branch on GitLab still names three retired linters in the project's
MegaLinter settings
GitLab shows the project's MegaLinter settings, .config/megalinter/config.yml, on the main branch. They still name three
linters MegaLinter has retired: REPOSITORY_GITLEAKS, SQL_TSQLLINT and REPOSITORY_KICS, two of them with options of their
own.
Around them sit the project's own choices: comments that explain its settings, two supported exclusions (JSON_V8R and
YAML_V8R) and two strict checks. A second settings file, config.flow.yml, writes its list on one bracketed block and
names REPOSITORY_GITLEAKS too.
Then the framework update stops at a settings file linked outside the project, before it
changes any MegaLinter setting
On their own machine, the developer has added a third settings file, shared.yml, and committed it without pushing. It is
a link: readlink shows it points to /workspace/shared/megalinter.yml, a file outside the project.
The developer asks for the framework update. Copier brings the new release in, then runs the MegaLinter clean-up, which
stops with "Refusing to migrate linked or external MegaLinter configuration". The task fails, so nothing is pushed and
no merge request opens.
git status lists the two files Copier had already written. No MegaLinter settings file is among them: the clean-up
checks every file before it changes any.
When the developer drops the link and asks for the framework update again
The developer goes back to what GitLab holds: the reset drops the commit with the link, and git clean removes the file
the stopped update had added. Then they ask for the update again.
This time the clean-up prints "removed retired references" for config.flow.yml and for config.yml, and the update ends
with "Opened merge request update-framework-devsecops → main."

text.tspan: git reset -q --hard origin/main && git clean -fdq && task devsecops:update

g.text: Then the merge request removes only the retired linters and keeps every explanation and
control
The Changes tab of that merge request on GitLab, four files. The first two are the release itself, folded here: the
version number in the answers file, and the one file this test release adds.
In both MegaLinter files, only the lines that name a retired linter go. A comment written at the end of such a line
stays, on a line of its own. JSON_V8R, YAML_V8R, FORMATTERS_DISABLE_ERRORS and ERROR_ON_MISSING_EXEC_BIT stay as they
were.
And asking for the update a second time leaves nothing to change
The developer, now on the update branch, asks for the update once more. Copier says "Keeping template version 1.0.1",
and the clean-up runs without removing anything.
The update ends with "Nothing to commit on update-framework-devsecops.": nothing is pushed, and the merge request stays
as it was.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 5 steps · 5 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
